topics.topic: Error contract for malformed relation arguments in `store.read_records` (is `internal_error` allowed vs only `unknown_reference`/handled elsewhere)
questions: When `store.read_records` is called with a malformed relation argument set (wrong/missing/extra args), must it return `internal_error`, or is `unknown_reference` the only allowed error?
Is `internal_error` for malformed relation arguments part of `store.read_records`' public error contract, or should such argument-shape failures be impossible/handled elsewhere?

quotes: A call that passes other arguments is a defect of its caller and answers `internal_error` — so does one that omits an argument its relation names or passes one of another kind; that defect is decided before any record is looked up.
judgement.why: The text explicitly defines malformed relation arguments for `store.read_records` as `internal_error`, so this is already decided.
